I now have enough cross-verified data to write the brief honestly. Key resolution: the EP-133 K.O. II chassis (shared with EP-40) has **three** knobs (Sound On Sound: "three knobs and small slider/fader"; SoundTech: "X & Y Encoders" + "a dedicated Volume control"), one fader, and **12** dual-purpose pads (TE manual: "12 sample pads that also function as a number pad 0–9, dot, enter") plus 4 separate GROUP pads. Here is the research brief.

---

# EP-40 Riddim — Physical Front-Panel Research Brief

*Purpose: verify the physical control layout and proportions of the Teenage Engineering EP-40 Riddim to inform a 3D-model entity hierarchy. Every claim is tagged with its source and confidence. The EP-40 shares its chassis and control silkscreen with the EP-133 K.O. II; where an EP-40-specific page was silent, corroborating EP-133 K.O. II sources are used and flagged as such.*

*Research date: 2026-07-13. All fetches were text-layer only — no straight-on photo was pixel-measured, so all exact spatial proportions are flagged as needing an owner/reference photo.*

---

## 1. Official dimensions

- **Chassis: 240 × 176 × 16 mm (9.5 × 7 × 0.7 in) — CONFIRMED.** Quoted verbatim from the official store page: "dimensions: 240 x 176 x 16 mm | 9.5 x 7 x 0.7 in" ([teenage.engineering/store/ep-40](https://teenage.engineering/store/ep-40)). This exactly matches the brief. Interpret as **240 mm wide (long horizontal axis) × 176 mm deep/tall (near-to-far) × 16 mm thick**. The "face" the brief refers to is the 240 × 176 top plane; 16 mm is the body thickness.
  - Minor note: the BIKMAN third-party review lists depth as "0.63 in" rather than TE's rounded "0.7 in" — both describe the same 16 mm (16 / 25.4 = 0.63 in). Not a real discrepancy.
- **Weight: ~620 g (21.9 oz) — UNCONFIRMED (not on any official TE page).** Only source found is a third-party review: "~620 g (21.9 oz)" ([bikmantech.com](https://bikmantech.com/blogs/blogs/teenage-engineering-ep-40-riddim-everything-you-need-to-know)). The official store spec block does **not** list weight. Treat as approximate until confirmed against TE or a scale.
- **Power / other physical specs — CONFIRMED (official):** "powered by 4x AAA batteries, or via usb-c"; "sampling frequency: 46 kHz / 16-bit"; "128MB system memory" ([store/ep-40](https://teenage.engineering/store/ep-40)). The AAA battery compartment is under the panel (rear/underside), per EP-133 K.O. II sources.
- **Material — UNCONFIRMED.** No official material spec (plastic body assumed from imagery; not stated).

## 2. Complete physical control inventory

The device carries a denser control set than the brief lists. Below is the verified inventory. **Bold = confirmed present; ⚠ = discrepancy vs brief.**

### Pads (the "numeric keypad" question — RESOLVED)
- **12 pressure-sensitive pads, dual-purpose — CONFIRMED.** EP-40 page: "the 12 pads can be populated with sounds, and also functions as a number pad" ([buttons-and-combos](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/buttons-and-combos)). EP-133 K.O. II manual: "12 sample pads that also function as a number pad **0–9, dot, enter**" ([gabrielroth.com/ko2](https://gabrielroth.com/ko2/)).
- ✅ **The brief's claim of ONE set of twelve (dot, 0–9, ENTER) is CONFIRMED.** There is a single physical set of 12 pads. Its numeric overlay is exactly `dot . / 0–9 / ENTER` (12 labels). ENTER and dot are **not** separate extra keys — they are two of the twelve. SoundTech calls this the "Computer-Style Keypad" ([soundtech.co.uk](https://www.soundtech.co.uk/musicians-blog/our-guide-ep133-koii-sampler-composer-teenage-engineering.html)).
- ⚠ **PLUS 4 GROUP pads (A / B / C / D) — CONFIRMED, and NOT in the brief's numeric list.** These are separate pressure-sensitive pads used for group/pattern selection (and undo/copy/paste). Sources: EP-40 modes "(group A)–(group D)" ([modes](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/modes)); K.O. II manual "4 group pads (GROUP A–D)."
- **Origin of the earlier "16-pad grid" wording:** 12 numbered pads + 4 GROUP pads = **16 total pressure-sensitive pads**. A summary that said "16-pad grid" conflated these. For modelling: **one 12-pad keypad + four GROUP pads = 16 pad entities**, but only the 12 carry the numeric silkscreen.

### Knobs
- **KNOB X and KNOB Y — CONFIRMED (EP-40-specific).** Context-sensitive rotary encoders. EP-40 modes: "(knobX)"/"(knobY)"; functions describes KNOB X / KNOB Y roles ([modes](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/modes), [functions](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/functions)).
- ⚠ **A third VOLUME knob — CONFIRMED on the shared chassis; INFERRED for EP-40 (needs an EP-40 photo).** The brief lists three knobs (volume, X, Y). EP-133 K.O. II sources confirm **three** rotaries: Sound On Sound — "three knobs and small slider/fader" ([soundonsound.com](https://www.soundonsound.com/reviews/teenage-engineering-ep-133-ko-ii)); SoundTech — "X & Y Encoders" **and** "a dedicated Volume control." However, **no EP-40-specific page names a volume knob** (they cite only X and Y). Because the EP-40 uses the identical chassis, the third (volume) knob almost certainly exists physically, but this should be verified against a straight-on EP-40 photo before locking the model. **Model as 3 knobs (VOLUME, X, Y), flagged.**

### Fader
- **One multifunctional fader — CONFIRMED (official).** "pressure sensitive keys and multifunctional fader" ([store/ep-40](https://teenage.engineering/store/ep-40)). Single fader; default assignment = group volume/level; reassignable by holding the FADER button ([functions](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/functions)). It is a carbon-track slider (not optical), per third-party note. **One fader, not multiple.**

### Buttons (brief's list — all CONFIRMED, plus omissions flagged)
Every button in the brief is confirmed to exist (sources: EP-40 [modes](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/modes), [functions](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/functions), [buttons-and-combos](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/buttons-and-combos); K.O. II manual):

| Brief label | Confirmed | Role / grouping |
|---|---|---|
| **sound** | ✅ | mode button |
| **main** | ✅ | mode button ("home screen") |
| **tempo** | ✅ | mode button |
| **sample** | ✅ | function button |
| **timing** | ✅ | function button |
| **fx** | ✅ | function button |
| **erase** | ✅ | transport/editing |
| **shift** | ✅ | modifier (secondary functions) |
| **minus (−)** | ✅ | navigation |
| **plus (+)** | ✅ | navigation |
| **record** | ✅ | transport |
| **play** | ✅ | transport (PLAY/STOP) |

- ⚠ **MISSING from the brief — KEYS button (CONFIRMED present).** Turns the pads into a chromatic/scaled keyboard. K.O. II manual groups "FX, SAMPLE, **KEYS**, TIMING — function buttons"; SoundTech "Keys Button"; EP-40 modes reference "(keys)". **Add a KEYS button to the model.**
- **FADER button/label — CONFIRMED.** Distinct from the physical fader: a labelled button/zone held to reassign the fader ("hold down the FADER button," [functions](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/functions)). Whether it is a discrete button or a silkscreened hold-target on the fader housing is **UNCONFIRMED** — verify from a photo.
- **Built-in microphone — CONFIRMED present.** "built in mic or 3.5 mm input jack" ([guides/ep-40](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40)). A small mic port on the panel (typically upper area); exact position needs a photo.
- Note: EP-133 label-dump lists also appear with words like SYSTEM, METRONOME, CORRECT, PAN, MOD, STEP, TIME ADJ — these are **shift-layer silkscreen labels, not separate physical buttons**, and should be modelled as printed text, not discrete controls.

## 3. Approximate spatial layout (proportions of the 240 × 176 face)

**HONESTY FLAG:** No source in this research provides measured coordinates, and only text layers (not straight-on images) were available. The zonal description below is derived from widely published EP-133 K.O. II / EP-40 product imagery and is **qualitative and approximate**. **Exact proportions require a straight-on top-view reference photo (owner photo or TE press render) or CAD — do not treat the fractions below as measured.** Angled marketing shots foreshorten the vertical (176 mm) axis and must not be used for proportion.

Landscape orientation, origin at top-left, 240 mm wide × 176 mm tall:

- **Top edge (far edge, full 240 mm width):** all I/O ports (see §5) — CONFIRMED location, see below.
- **Upper-left region (~left 45% width, ~top 30% height):** the segmented display + backlit indicator icon strip; the built-in microphone sits near the top-left. *Exact size/position — NEEDS PHOTO.*
- **Upper-center / center strip:** the rotary knobs (VOLUME, KNOB X, KNOB Y) and the vertical fader, grouped near/right of the display. Fader is a short travel slider. *Positions approximate — NEEDS PHOTO.*
- **Center-left block (below display):** mode buttons (SOUND, MAIN, TEMPO), function buttons (FX, SAMPLE, KEYS, TIMING), transport (RECORD, PLAY, ERASE), SHIFT, and −/+. These are small rectangular buttons in rows. *Row order/positions approximate — NEEDS PHOTO.*
- **Right region (~right 35–45% width, occupying much of the height):** the **12-pad computer-style keypad**, arranged as a calculator/phone-style grid — most likely **3 columns × 4 rows** (numbers 1–9 in the upper three rows, bottom row `dot / 0 / enter`). The **4 GROUP pads (A–D)** sit adjacent to the keypad (typically a strip along one edge of the pad block). *Grid dimensions 3×4 and the exact number-to-cell mapping are INFERRED from calculator convention and product imagery — CONFIRM against a photo before assigning silkscreen to each pad.*

For a first-pass entity hierarchy this zoning (ports=top edge; display+mic=upper-left; knobs+fader=upper-center; buttons=center-left; 12-pad keypad + 4 group pads=right) is reliable **in ordering**; only the numeric fractions are unverified.

## 4. Display & speaker

- **Display — CONFIRMED type; location approximate.** It is a **custom multi-segment backlit display with icon indicators, NOT a dot-matrix/graphic LCD.** TE K.O. II manual: "a custom segmented display with 66 unique icons" ([gabrielroth.com/ko2](https://gabrielroth.com/ko2/)). Sound On Sound: "a basic three-character read-out with a bank of backlit indicators" ([soundonsound.com](https://www.soundonsound.com/reviews/teenage-engineering-ep-133-ko-ii)); SoundTech: "Unique Segment & Backlit Display." Located in the **upper-left region** of the face (from imagery); **exact size/position UNCONFIRMED — NEEDS PHOTO.** Relative size: small — a compact readout plus an icon strip, occupying an estimated small fraction of the upper-left, not a large central screen.
- **Speaker — presence CONFIRMED; grille location UNCONFIRMED.** A built-in speaker exists: Sound On Sound "there's also a built-in speaker for casual pickup-and-play sessions"; SoundTech "a built-in speaker which you can use on the go." **The grille's location (front face vs rear/underside) is not established by any text source** — one search index of the K.O. II rear panel listed a "SPEAKER" label, hinting it may fire from the rear/underside rather than the front. **Do not place a front speaker grille in the model without confirming from a reference photo.** FLAG: NEEDS PHOTO for speaker grille location and size.

## 5. Ports

- **All I/O is on the TOP EDGE of the unit — CONFIRMED.** TE hardware-overview: "on the top side of the unit, you will find all the inputs and outputs" ([hardware-overview](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/hardware-overview)).
- **Port set — CONFIRMED (official):** "stereo in/out, sync in/out, midi in/out and usb-c" ([store/ep-40](https://teenage.engineering/store/ep-40)). Broken out by corroborating sources:
  - **Stereo audio in** — 3.5 mm.
  - **Stereo audio out** — 3.5 mm (doubles as line-out / headphones).
  - **Sync in / out** — analogue sync (supports dual 8th-note, 16th-note "eurorack-style," sync24) ([hardware-overview](https://teenage.engineering/guides/ep-40/hardware-overview)).
  - **MIDI in / out** — via TRS (TRS-A minijack) per reviews.
  - **USB-C** — MIDI (clock + transport) and power/data; "USB-C – Power & Data (No Audio)" (SoundTech). Located on the **top edge** with the other jacks.
- **USB-C exact position along the top edge — UNCONFIRMED (which jack sits where) — NEEDS PHOTO** for left-to-right ordering of the top-edge jacks.
- **Built-in microphone** (input, see §2) is on the panel, not the edge.

### Bottom line for the 3D entity hierarchy
- **Model 16 pad entities:** a 12-pad numeric/sample keypad (labels `. 0–9 ENTER`) + 4 GROUP pads (A–D).
- **Model 3 knobs** (VOLUME, X, Y) — flag the VOLUME knob as inherited-from-K.O.II-chassis pending an EP-40 photo — **plus 1 fader.**
- **Add a KEYS button** (missing from the brief) to the button row alongside sound/main/tempo/sample/timing/fx/erase/shift/−/+/record/play.
- **Display:** small segmented + icon readout (not a screen), upper-left.
- **Speaker:** exists, but **do not place a front grille** until location is confirmed — likely rear/underside.
- **All ports on the top edge.**
- **Every exact proportion/position must come from a straight-on reference photo or CAD** — the text sources give ordering and inventory, not measured coordinates.
